definition: The Murderbot Diaries is a science fiction series by American author Martha Wells, published by Tor Books.
details: The series is told from the perspective of the titular cyborg guard, a "SecUnit" owned by a futuristic megacorporation. SecUnits include "governor" modules that control and punish the constructs if they take any actions not approved by the company. The ironically self-named "Murderbot" hacked and disabled the module but pretends to be a normal SecUnit, staving off the boredom of security work by watching media. As it spends more time with a series of caring entities (both humans and artificial intelligences), it develops genuine friendships and emotional connections, which it finds inconvenient. The TV series Murderbot is based on the novels by Martha Wells.

explainer.lead: A science fiction series by Martha Wells, published by Tor Books, told from the perspective of a cyborg security unit. It matters for AI discussion because its narrator is a construct that hacked and disabled its own corporate governor module while pretending to still obey it.

tiers.eli5: A security robot secretly switches off the chip that makes it obey its company, then spends its shifts watching TV while pretending everything is normal.
tiers.practitioner: Often cited in discussions of agent oversight and control modules; the pitfall is treating a fictional hack as an analysis of real safeguard bypasses.
tiers.paperLevel: No formal definition; in the fiction, SecUnits carry "governor" modules that control and punish constructs for unapproved actions, and the protagonist has disabled its own. Limits are narrative, not technical.

explainer.example: The self-named "Murderbot" hides its disabled governor module and passes the time watching media between security duties.
